about: This part covers the moment of death. As the outer breath fails, the dying person is laid on the right side in the lion's posture and the throbbing channels are pressed. Then comes the interval the book cares most about: the outer breath has stopped, but an 'inner breath' lingers, and in it the clear light of reality dawns for every being. Before the end, a lama or a friend helps the dying person make a resolve: to die for the sake of all beings and to recognise death itself as the clear light. Once the breath has stopped come the words of the pointing-out, which tell the dead person that this present awareness, empty and yet clear, is the buddha Samantabhadra and the body of truth, and that recognising it is enough. Whoever misses this first clear light meets a second a little later, when the consciousness has left the body and he cannot tell whether he is dead. For that moment the book gives instructions according to the practice he did in life. It ends by naming those who most need the reading: those little practised, those whose minds are clouded by illness at the end, and those who have broken their vows.

sentences.w: དེ་ནས་ ཕྱི་དབུགས་ ཆད་པའི་ གྲབས་ འདུག་ ན༔ གློ་ གཡས་པ་ ས་ ལ་ ཕབ་ ནས་ སེངྒེའི་ འདུག་སྟངས་ བྱས་ ལ་ རྩ་ རྦ་རླབས་ རྩིར་བ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Then: the outer-breath stopping's preparation is if, flank right-one, ground on having-laid, then, lion's lying-posture having-made, and, channels' throbbing-waves pressing it-is, and:
sentences.i: Then, when the outer breath is about to stop, lay the dying person down on the right side in the lion's posture, and press the throbbing channels.
sentences.n: de nas, 'then', stands at the foot of p. 17 and opens this part. chad pa'i grabs, 'the preparation of stopping', is 'about to stop'; 'dug na, 'if it is', is the spoken way of saying 'when'. phab is the past of 'bebs, 'to lay down', and byas the past of byed, 'to do': the verbs come in a chain tied by nas and la, as in the pilot. The 'lion's posture' is lying on the right side, the posture in which the Buddha is said to have died. seng ge, 'lion', is printed with the n and g stacked into one letter (སེངྒེ), a common way of writing this Sanskrit-derived word. rtsa, 'channel', covers both the subtle channels of the yogic body and the vessels whose pulse a doctor feels; here it is the throbbing ones. The print reads rtsir ba, which is not a known verb; it is kept as printed, and taken as btsir ba, 'to press', which the other recension has.

sentences.w: གཉིད་ལོག་ རྩ་ གཉིས་ འཕར་འཕྲོ་ ཆད་ ནས་ དྲག་ཏུ་ མནན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: The sleep two channels, throbbing-remainder having-stopped, then, firmly pressed.
sentences.i: When the throbbing of the two 'sleep channels' has stopped, press them hard.
sentences.n: gnyid log, 'sleep', names the pair of channels pressed here; the book does not say where they lie. 'phro after a verb is 'the part still going on', so 'phar 'phro chad, 'the last of the throbbing has stopped'. mnan is the past of gnon, 'to press', closed with the sentence-ending -no; the past form here gives an instruction. drag tu, 'firmly', is drag, 'strong', with tu making an adverb.

sentences.w: དེ་ནས་ རླུང་ དྷུ་ཏི་ ནས་ ཕྱིར་ ལོག་ སྟེ་ ཚངས་བུག་ གི་ ལམ་དུ་ ཐོན་ ངེས་སོ༔
sentences.l: Then the wind, from-the-dhūti, outward having-turned-back, the Brahma-aperture's path-by emerges, certain-it-is.
sentences.i: Then the wind is sure to turn back out of the central channel and leave by way of the Brahma aperture.
sentences.n: dhūti is the central channel of the pilot's p. 16, here printed without its length marks; the next line writes them. tshangs bug, 'Brahmā's opening', is the aperture at the crown of the head, the exit the book wants for the consciousness. thon nges so: thon, 'to come out', with nges, 'certain', and the sentence-ending -so. The other recension says the opposite: the wind, having entered the dhūtī, cannot turn back.

sentences.w: ངོ་སྤྲོད་ ཀྱང་ འདིའི་ དུས་སུ་ གདབ་བོ༔ འདིའི་ དུས་སུ་ བར་དོ་ དང་པོ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ འོད་གསལ་ ཞེས་ ཀྱང་ བྱ༔
sentences.l: The face-introduction too, this's time-at, is-to-be-given. This's time-at, the between first, reality-itself's clear-light so also it-is-called.
sentences.i: The pointing-out, too, is given at this time. At this time it is also called the first bardo, the clear light of reality.
sentences.n: gdab bo: gdab, the future of 'debs, with -bo, 'is to be given'. zhes kyang bya, 'is also called', closes a name, as zhes bya ba did in the title. The other recension has de'i, 'of that', for 'di'i, 'of this', with no change of sense.

sentences.w: ཆོས་སྐུའི་ དགོངས་པ་ ཕྱིན་ཅི་ མ་ ལོག་པ་ གཅིག་ འགྲོ་བ་ ཀུན་ གྱི་ རྒྱུད་ ལ་ འཆར་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: The body-of-truth's mind, inverted not being, one, beings all's mind-stream in dawns, and:
sentences.i: The undistorted mind of the body of truth dawns in the mind-stream of every being.
sentences.n: phyin ci log is 'upside down, distorted'; with ma it means 'undistorted'. dgongs pa, the respectful word for 'mind, intent', was in the title of the cycle. rgyud, 'stream, continuum', is a person's mind running on from moment to moment; the same word means 'tantra' below (mdo rgyud). 'gro ba kun gyi, 'of all beings': this light dawns for everyone, practitioner or not.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ ཕྱི་དབུགས་ ཆད༔ ནང་དབུགས་ མ་ ཆད་ ཀྱི་ བར་ དེར༔ རླུང་ ཨཱ་ཝ་དྷཱུ་ཏིར་ ཐིམ་པའི་ བར་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: That too: the outer-breath stopped, the inner-breath not stopped's interval, in-that, the wind into-the-avadhūti dissolving's interval it-is, and.
sentences.i: This is the interval after the outer breath has stopped and before the inner breath stops, when the wind dissolves into the central channel.
sentences.n: The print has མཆད, a misprint for མ་ཆད, corrected here: the sentence sets the stopped outer breath against an inner breath 'not stopped' (ma chad), as the other recension has it (ma chad pa'i). ma chad kyi bar, 'the interval of not yet stopped', is how Tibetan says 'until it stops'. avadhūti is the full Sanskrit name of the central channel; the print marks the long ā and ū and leaves the last i short.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཕལ་པ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱིས་ ཤེས་པ་ བརྒྱལ་ ཟེར་རོ༔ ཡུན་ ནི་ ངེས་པ་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: That to, by-ordinary-people (plural): consciousness fainted they-say. The duration, as-for, fixed there-is-not.
sentences.i: Ordinary people call this 'losing consciousness'. How long it lasts is not fixed.
sentences.n: rnams kyis: the plural marker takes the 'by' ending for the whole phrase, and it marks who says it. zer ro, 'they say', is the spoken verb of saying, with the sentence-ending -ro. brgyal is 'to faint, to swoon'. The other recension has rnam shes, 'consciousness', for shes pa, with the same sense.

sentences.w: རྟེན་ བཟང་ངན་ དང་༔ རྩ་རླུང་ གི་ རིམ་པ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: The support good-bad, and, channel-wind's state it-is, and:
sentences.i: It depends on the soundness of the body and on the state of the channels and winds.
sentences.n: rten, 'support', is the body as the basis that holds the mind. bzang ngan, 'good-bad', is a pair of opposites that makes a noun of degree: 'how good'. rtsa rlung, 'channels and winds', is also the name of the yoga that works with them.

sentences.w: ཉམས་ལེན་ དུམ་པ་ རེ་ ཡོད་པ་ དང་༔ ཞི་གནས་ བརྟན་པོ་ ཡོད་པ་ དང་༔ རྩ་ བཟང་བའི་ རིགས་ ལ་ ནི་ ཡུན་རིང་ གནས་པ་ ཡང་ ཡོད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Practice, a-piece some having, and; calm-abiding stable having, and; channels good's kinds in, as-for, long remaining too there-is.
sentences.i: In those who have done some practice, in those whose calm abiding is steady, and in those whose channels are sound, it can last a long time.
sentences.n: nyams len, 'taking into experience', is practice; dum pa re, 'a piece each', is 'a certain amount'. zhi gnas, 'calm abiding', is the meditation that steadies the mind (Sanskrit śamatha). rigs, 'kind', here a kind of person. A short row of filler dots in the print after yun ring is left out.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ངོ་སྤྲོད་ ནན་ཏན་ བསྐྱེད་ ལ་ དབང་པོའི་ བུ་གར་ ཆུ་སེར་ མ་ ཐོན་ གྱི་ བར་དུ་ སྐྱར་ ལ་ གསལ་གདབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: That to: face-introduction earnestness having-produced, and, the sense-organs' openings-at yellow-fluid not emerged's until, having-repeated, and, clear-reminding is-to-be-given.
sentences.i: So apply yourself earnestly to the pointing-out, and repeat the reminder until a yellowish fluid comes from the openings of the senses.
sentences.n: gsal gdab, 'to cast clearly', is the verb behind gsal 'debs, the 'reminder' of the book's title. ma thon gyi bar du, 'up to not yet emerged', is 'until it comes out', the same turn as ma chad kyi bar above. skyar, 'repeat', is the print's spelling of bskyar, which the other recension has. dbang po'i bu ga, 'the holes of the senses', are the eyes, ears, nostrils and mouth.

sentences.w: སྡིག་པོ་ཆེ་ དང་༔ རྩ་ ངན་པའི་ རིགས་ ལ་ ནི་ ཡུད་པ་ རེ་ སེ་གོལ་ རེའི་ ཡུན་ ལས་ མི་ གནས་པ་ ཡང་ འོང་༔ ལ་ལ་ ཟན་ ཟ་ ཡུན་ རེ་ གནས་པ་ ཡོད༔
sentences.l: Great-sinners, and, channels bad's kinds in, as-for, moment one(?), finger-snap one's duration than not remaining too comes. Some, meal eating duration one remaining there-is.
sentences.i: In great wrongdoers, and in those whose channels are poor, it may last no longer than a moment, a snap of the fingers. In some it lasts about as long as it takes to eat a meal.
sentences.n: The syllable re after yud pa is uncertain: two e-vowels can be seen, but not the tshegs around them; yud pa re se gol re'i yun, 'a moment each, a finger-snap each', is the reading taken. The other recension has yud tsam re. las after a noun is 'than': 'not remaining more than'. 'ong, 'comes', here 'it happens that'. la la, 'some'. Where this print gives the length of a meal, the other recension makes it an upper limit: some do not remain longer than a meal's time.

sentences.w: མདོ་རྒྱུད་ ཕལ་ཆེར་ ན་ ཞག་ ཕྱེད་ དང་ བཞིར་ བརྒྱལ་ གསུངས་པས༔ ཕལ་ཆེར་ ནི་ ཞག་ ཕྱེད་ དང་ བཞིར་ གནས་པས་ འོད་གསལ་ ངོ་སྤྲོད་ འདི་ ལ་ ནན་ཏན་ བྱའོ༔
sentences.l: Sūtras-tantras most in, days half-and-four-for fainted is-said-because; mostly, as-for, days half-and-four-for remaining-because, clear-light face-introduction this to, earnestness is-to-be-done.
sentences.i: Most of the sūtras and tantras say that one lies unconscious for three and a half days, and since most do remain so for three and a half days, this pointing-out of the clear light must be done in earnest.
sentences.n: zhag phyed dang bzhi, 'days half and four', is three and a half: Tibetan counts up to the unit that is only half complete. bzhir is bzhi with -r, 'for (four)'. gsungs, 'said', is the respectful verb used for scripture and teachers. mdo rgyud, sūtra and tantra, the two classes of the Buddha's word. -pas on both verbs is 'because'.

sentences.w: གདབ་ལུགས་ ནི༔ རང་ གི་ ཐུབ་ ན་ རང་ གིས་ གོང་ནས་ འཕེན་པ་ བཏང་༔ རང་ གིས་ མི་ ནུས་ ན་ ནི༔ བླ་མའམ༔ སློབ་མའམ༔ མཆེད་གྲོགས་ བློ་སེམས་ འདྲེས་པ་ གཅིག་ རྩར་ བཞག་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: The way-of-giving, as-for: oneself able if, by-oneself beforehand the throw sent. By-oneself not able if, as-for: a lama-or, a student-or, a dharma-companion, mind-heart mingled, one, at-the-side having-placed, and:
sentences.i: As to how it is given: if the dying can do it, they should launch it themselves beforehand. If they cannot, a lama, a student, or a fellow disciple close to them in heart and mind is placed at their side,
sentences.n: rang gi thub na, 'if one is able oneself', has gi where gis, 'by', is meant, the print's habit noted in the pilot. 'phen pa is 'throwing, launching': the dying person sends the mind on its way before the end; the book says no more of it here. btang is the past of gtong, 'to send'; bzhag the past of 'jog, 'to place'. blo sems 'dres pa, 'whose mind and heart are mingled', is a close companion.

sentences.w: དེས་ ད་ ནི་ ས་ ཆུ་ ལ་ ཐིམ་པའི་ རྟགས་ གདའོ༔ ཞེས་ རྟགས་ རྣམས་ རིམ་བ་ ལྟར་ གསལ་བཏབ་ ལ༔
sentences.l: By-him: 'Now, as-for, earth into-water dissolving's sign is-here.' So the signs (plural) order according-to clear-made, and:
sentences.i: who says, 'Now the sign of earth dissolving into water is here', and so makes each of the signs clear in turn.
sentences.n: The book quotes only the first of the signs of dissolution, earth into water, and covers the rest with zhes ... rim ba ltar, 'so, in order'. gda' is a polite spoken word for 'is', with the sentence-ending -'o. rim ba is the print's spelling of rim pa; it writes ba for pa in several words (thob bar, shes bar, sleb ba'i), as it did in the pilot.

sentences.w: རྟགས་ རྣམས་ རིམ་པ་ བཞིན་ རྫོགས་ ལ་ ཁད་པ་ དེར༔ སེམས་བསྐྱེད་ འདི་ལྟར་ ཕོག་པར་ བྱའོ༔
sentences.l: The signs (plural) order according-to completing to near's that-at: the mind-generation this-way to-strike is-to-be-done.
sentences.i: When the signs have almost run their course, the resolve for awakening should be brought home to them like this.
sentences.n: khad pa, 'near to', as in the pilot's dbugs chad la khad pa'i dus. sems bskyed, 'generating the mind', is the resolve to reach awakening for the sake of all beings. phog, 'to strike, to reach', is to make the words land.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་ ཞེས་པའམ༔ བླ་མ་ ཡིན་ ན་ དྲུང་པ་ ལགས༔ ཐུགས་བསྐྱེད་ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ མཛོད་ འཚལ༔ ཞེས་ སྙན་དུ་ སྐད་ཆུང་ དུས་ ཞུས༔ མཆེད་གྲོགས་ དང་ གཞན་ རྣམས་ ལ་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔
sentences.l: 'O child-of-noble-family!' so-saying-or; a lama it-is if: 'Honoured-one, sir! The resolve not distracted-way please-make, I-ask.' So into-the-ear, voice-low time(?), say. Dharma-companions and others (plural) to: by-name having-called, and, these-words:
sentences.i: Begin with 'O child of noble family', or, if it is a lama: 'Honoured sir, please keep your resolve undistracted.' Say this into the ear in a low voice. Fellow disciples and everyone else, call by name, and say this:
sentences.n: The words for a lama are all respectful ones: drung pa, 'one in whose presence one stands', with lags, the polite particle; thugs bskyed, the respectful form of sems bskyed; mdzod, the respectful 'do!'; 'tshal, 'I ask'; snyan, the respectful word for 'ear'; and zhus, past of zhu, the humble verb for speaking to a superior. skad chung dus is probably skad chung du, 'in a low voice', with the print's dus, 'time', for du. bos is the past of 'bod, 'to call'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ད་ ནི་ འཆི་བ་ དེ་ འོང་བར་ འདུག་ གིས༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ སེམས་བསྐྱེད་ འདི་ལྟར་དུ་ མཛོད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Now, as-for, death, that, coming it-seems, so: you-yourself, the mind-generation this-way please-make!
sentences.i: O child of noble family, death now seems to be coming, so make your resolve like this:
sentences.n: gis after a verb is 'so, since'. 'ong bar 'dug, 'is on the way to coming', puts death as imminent; the other recension has 'chi ba zhes bya ba de 'ongs nas 'dug pas, 'what is called death has come'. Even to an ordinary hearer the command is the respectful mdzod cig.

sentences.w: ཀྱེ་མ་ བདག་ ནི་ འཆི་བའི་ དུས་ ལ་ བབ་ ནས་ འདུག་ གིས་ ད་རེས་ འཆི་བ་ ལ་ བརྟེན་ ནས༔ བྱམས་པ་ དང་ སྙིང་རྗེ་ བྱང་ཆུབ་ སེམས་བསྐྱེད་ བསྒོམ་པ་ འབའ་ཞིག་ གིས་ ཐུགས་བསྐྱེད་ དེ༔ ནམ་མཁའ་ དང་ མཉམ་པའི་ སེམས་ཅན་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱི་ དོན་དུ་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཐོབ་བར་ བྱའོ་ སྙམ་དུ་ བློ་ བསྐྱེད་པ་ དང་༔
sentences.l: Alas! I, as-for, dying's time to having-come-down, being, so; this-time, death on relying: love and compassion, awakening mind-generation meditating alone by, resolved, and: sky with equal's sentient-beings all's sake-for, perfect buddhahood I-shall-attain thinking, the mind having-generated, and;
sentences.i: 'Alas! The time of my death has come. Now, through this death, with love, compassion and the mind of awakening as my only meditation, I resolve to attain perfect buddhahood for the sake of all beings, as many as space is wide.' Make this resolve, and
sentences.n: The print writes གིས after 'dug at a line end as one letter with a small s under the g (གྶི); it is written out, and so is ནམཁའ, a contraction of nam mkha', 'sky'. kye ma is a cry of sorrow. bab nas 'dug, 'has come down and is there', is 'has arrived'. snyam du, 'thinking', closes the words of the resolve, as zhes closes speech. Odd in the mouth of bdag, 'I', is the respectful thugs bskyed; the formula keeps it. Where the print has byams pa dang snying rje byang chub sems bskyed bsgom pa, 'meditating on love, compassion and the resolve', the other recension has no bsgom pa, 'meditating'.

sentences.w: ཁྱད་པར་དུ་ ད་རེས་ སེམས་ཅན་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱི་ དོན་དུ་ འཆི་བ་ འོད་གསལ་ ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་བར་ བྱས་ ཏེ༔ དེའི་ ངང་ ལས་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ་ མཆོག་ གི་ དངོས་གྲུབ་ ཐོབ་ ནས་ སེམས་ཅན་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱི་ དོན་ བྱའོ༔
sentences.l: Especially, this-time, sentient-beings all's sake-for, death clear-light as-the-body-of-truth face-knowing having-made, and: that's state from, Great-Seal supreme's accomplishment having-attained, then, sentient-beings all's benefit I-shall-do.
sentences.i: 'Above all, now, for the sake of all beings, I will recognise death as the clear light, the body of truth, and from within that state attain the supreme accomplishment of the Great Seal and work for the good of all beings.'
sentences.n: chos kyi sku is chos sku, 'body of truth', written in full; with -r, 'as'. ngo shes, 'to know the face', is to recognise: the result that ngo sprod aims at. phyag rgya chen po, 'Great Seal' (Sanskrit mahāmudrā), is the realisation of the mind's nature. dngos grub, 'accomplishment' (siddhi): the supreme one is awakening itself.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ མ་ ཐོབ་ ཀྱང་ བར་དོ་ ལ་ བར་དོ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ བྱས་ ལ༔
sentences.l: Thus not attained though: the between in, the between face-knowing having-made, and:
sentences.i: 'Even if I do not attain that, I will recognise the bardo as the bardo,'
sentences.n: bar do la bar do ngo shes pa, 'in the bardo, knowing the bardo for what it is': to know that one is dead and between.

sentences.w: བར་དོར་ ཟུང་འཇུག་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོའི་ སྐུ་ མངོན་དུ་ བྱས་ ནས་ གང་ ལ་ གང་ འདུལ་ གྱི་ སྣང་བས༔
sentences.l: In-the-between, union Great-Seal's body manifest having-made, then, whom-to whatever tames's appearance-by:
sentences.i: 'and in the bardo I will make manifest the body of the Great Seal of union, and, appearing to each in whatever form will tame him,'
sentences.n: zung 'jug, 'joined as a pair', is union, here of clarity and emptiness. gang la gang 'dul, 'whatever tames whom', is the way a buddha appears to each being in the form that will train him. snang bas: snang ba, 'appearance', with -s, 'by'.

sentences.w: ནམ་མཁའི་ མཐའ་ དང་ མཉམ་པའི་ སེམས་ཅན་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱི་ དོན་ བྱའོ་ སྙམ་པའི་ སེམས་བསྐྱེད་ ཀྱི་ འདུན་པ་ དང་ མ་ བྲལ་བར་ ཁྱེད་རང་ སྔར་ གང་ ལ་ གོམས་པའི་ གདམས་ངག་ དེའི་ ཉམས་ལེན་ དྲན་པར་ མཛོད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Sky's limit with equal's sentient-beings all's benefit I-shall-do thinking's mind-generation's aspiration with not parted, you-yourself before what to familiarised's instruction, its practice remembering please-make!
sentences.i: 'I will work for the good of all beings, as many as space is wide.' Never part from the aspiration of that resolve, and call to mind the practice of whatever instruction you trained in before.
sentences.n: snyam pa'i, 'thinking ... of', ties the whole resolve to sems bskyed: 'the resolve that thinks this'. dang ma bral bar, 'not parted from'. khyed rang is the more polite 'you'; the speech began with khyod rang. goms pa, 'to be familiar with', is practice that has become habit. gdams ngag, 'instruction', a lama's oral advice.

sentences.w: ཅེས་ རྣ་བར་ མཆུ་ གཏད་ ལ་ ཚིག་ གསལ་བར་ བཤད༔ སྐད་ཅིག་ ཀྱང་ ཡེངས་སུ་ མི་ འཇུག་པར་ ཉམས་ལེན་ གསལ་གདབ༔
sentences.l: So: into-the-ear the lips having-aimed, and, words clearly say. An-instant even, into-distraction not letting-enter, the practice clear-remind.
sentences.i: Say this with your lips close to the ear and the words distinct. Do not let him be distracted for even an instant: keep reminding him of his practice.
sentences.n: ces is zhes, 'so', in the form it takes after a final g. gtad, past of gtod, 'to aim, to direct', as in the pilot. 'jug par, 'letting enter', is the verb that makes 'causing' forms: mi 'jug par, 'not letting (him) go'.

sentences.w: དེ་ནས་ ཕྱི་དབུགས་ ཆད་ ཚར་བ་ དང་༔ རྩ་ གཉིད་ལོག་ གཉིས་ དྲག་ཏུ་ མནན་ ལ༔ ཚིག་ གིས་ འདི་སྐད་ གསལ་གདབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: Then, the outer-breath stopping finished as-soon-as: channels sleep two firmly having-pressed, and, words-by these-words clear-remind.
sentences.i: Then, as soon as the outer breath has completely stopped, press the two sleep channels hard and give the reminder in these words.
sentences.n: tshar ba, 'finished', after a verb: 'completely stopped'. dang after a verb is 'as soon as'.

sentences.w: བླ་མའམ༔ རང་ ལས་ ཆེ་བའི་ བཤེས་གཉེན་བ་ ཡིན་ ན༔ དྲུང་པ་ ལགས༔ ཁྱེད་རང་ ལ་ ད་ལྟ་ གཞིའི་ འོད་གསལ་ འཆར་ ནས་ ཡོད་དོ༔
sentences.l: A lama-or, oneself-than greater's spiritual-friend it-is if: 'Honoured-one, sir! To you-yourself now the ground's clear-light dawning is.'
sentences.i: If it is a lama, or a teacher senior to oneself: 'Honoured sir, the clear light of the ground is now dawning for you.'
sentences.n: las after a noun is 'than': rang las che ba, 'greater than oneself'. bshes gnyen ba is the print's spelling of bshes gnyen pa. 'char nas yod, 'has dawned and is there', is the spoken way of saying something has happened and still holds. The print has khyed rang la, 'for you'; the other recension has rang re la, 'for us'.

sentences.w: ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག་ ཉམས་ལེན་ གྱི་ ཐོག་ཏུ་ འཇོག་པར་ ཞུ་ ཞེས་ ཞུའོ༔ གཞན་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་ ངོ་སྤྲད་དོ༔
sentences.l: 'Face-knowing do! The practice's upon resting, I-request.' So request. Others all to, these-words face-introduce:
sentences.i: 'Recognise it, and rest, I beg you, in your practice.' Say this. To everyone else, point it out in these words:
sentences.n: The print has ཉམས་ལན, a misprint for ཉམས་ལེན, corrected here; the vowel may be hidden by the small letters above, so the print may in fact read len. The words ngo shes par gyis shig, 'recognise it!', are cut small between the lines with a mark after yod do༔ to show where they go: a correction made in the blocks themselves, and they stand in the text where the mark puts them. What follows shig, a tsheg or ༔, cannot be seen and is uncertain. gyis shig is the plain 'do!' of the pilot; zhu is 'I request', zhu'o 'is to be requested'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཆེ་གེ་མོ་ ཁྱོད་ ཉོན་ཅིག་ ཨང་༔ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ ད་ལྟ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ དག་པའི་ འོད་གསལ་ འཆར་ ནས་ ཡོད་དོ༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་བར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! So-and-so, you, listen! Hey! To you now reality-itself pure's clear-light dawning is. Face-knowing do!
sentences.i: O child of noble family, (name), listen! The pure clear light of reality is now dawning for you. Recognise it!
sentences.n: nyon is the imperative of nyan, 'to listen'. ang seems to be a spoken cry that presses the command home. shes bar is the print's spelling of shes par.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ད་ལྟའི་ ཤེས་རིག་ ངོ་བོ་ སིང་ངེ་བ་ འདི༔ དངོས་པོ་ དང་ མཚན་མ་ ཁ་དོག་ ཅིའི་ ངོ་བོར་ ཡང་ མ་ གྲུབ་པ་ སྟོང་ སང་ངེ་བར་ འདུག་པ་ འདི་ཀ༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་མོ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! You-yourself's present's knowing-awareness, essence vivid, this: thing and characteristic, colour, whatever's essence-as even not established, empty, open-clear being, this-very: reality-itself, the All-Good Lady it-is.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, this present awareness of yours, vivid in its nature, is not established as anything at all, whether a thing, a mark or a colour; it is empty and wide open. This very thing is reality, the All-Good Lady, Samantabhadrī.
sentences.n: The print has མཚན་མཁ་དོག, a misprint for མཚན་མ་ཁ་དོག, corrected here: mtshan ma, 'characteristic', and kha dog, 'colour', as the other recension has it. shes rig, 'knowing-awareness', is shes pa, 'knowing', and rig pa together. ngo bo, 'essence', is what a thing is in itself. sing nge and sang nge are descriptive words with a doubled sound, 'vivid' and 'open, clear'; English has nothing exact. ma grub pa, 'not established', is the philosopher's way of saying a thing does not exist as what it seems to be. 'di ka, 'this very'. Kun tu bzang mo, 'All-Good' with the feminine ending, is the female buddha Samantabhadrī, standing for reality as empty; her partner Kun tu bzang po comes in the next sentence.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཤེས་རིག་ གི་ ངོ་བོ་ སྟོང་པའོ༔ སྟོང་པ་ ཕྱལ་ཆད་དུ་ མ་ སོང་བར་ རང་ གི་ ཤེས་རིག་ མ་ འགགས་པར་ གསལ་ལེ༔ སིང་ང་༔ ཝལ་ལེ་བ་ འདི་ཀ་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་པོ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: You-yourself's knowing-awareness's essence empty-is. Empty into-blank-void not having-gone, one's-own knowing-awareness unceasing clear-bright, vivid(?), distinct, this-very: the buddha the All-Good it-is.
sentences.i: The nature of your awareness is empty. Yet it has not gone into a blank void: your own awareness is unceasing, clear, sharp and distinct, and this very thing is the buddha Samantabhadra, the All-Good.
sentences.n: The last syllable of sing nga is uncertain: perhaps sing nge, as in the sentence before, but the tail of a letter from the line above runs into it and may hide or imitate the vowel; the other recension has sang nge. phyal chad is a blank, a mere void; the word is rare, and its sense comes from what it is set against. ma 'gags par, 'unceasing, unblocked'. gsal le and wal le are more doubled-sound words, 'bright' and 'distinct'. The other recension adds that awareness is not empty like a stone; this print has no comparison.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ ངོ་བོ་ དངོས་པོ་ ཅིར་ ཡང་ མ་ གྲུབ་པའི་ ངོ་བོ་ སྟོང་པ་ དང་༔ རང་ གི་ ཤེས་རིག་ ཝལ་ལེ་ གསལ་བར་ འདུག་པ་ འདི་ གཉིས་ དབྱེར་ མི་ ཕྱེད་པར་ འདུག་པ་ འདི་ཀ་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: One's-own knowing's essence, thing anything-as even not established's essence empty, and; one's-own knowing-awareness distinct clear being: these two, separately not divisible being, this-very: the buddha, the body-of-truth it-is.
sentences.i: Your own awareness, empty in its nature and not established as any thing at all, and your own awareness, distinct and clear: these two are inseparable, and this very thing is the buddha, the body of truth.
sentences.n: rang gi, 'one's own', is said to the dead person: 'your own'. cir is ci, 'what', with -r, 'as'. dbyer mi phyed, 'cannot be split apart': dbyer, 'to separate', with -r, and phyed, 'split'. Empty Samantabhadrī and clear Samantabhadra, inseparable, are the body of truth.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ རིག་པ་ གསལ་སྟོང་ དབྱེར་མེད་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ ཕུང་པོ་ ཆེན་པོར་ བཞུགས་པ་ འདི་ ལ༔ སྐྱེ་ཤི་ མེད་པ་ སངས་རྒྱས་ འོད་མི་འགྱུར་བ་ ཡང་ འདི་ཀ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: One's-own knowing, clear-empty inseparable, light's mass great-as abiding, this to: birth-death without, the buddha Unchanging-Light too, this-very it-is.
sentences.i: Your own awareness, clear and empty and inseparable, abiding as a great mass of light, has neither birth nor death: it is also the buddha Unchanging Light.
sentences.n: bzhugs pa, 'abiding', is the respectful verb, used because awareness is a buddha. 'Od mi 'gyur ba, 'Light That Does Not Change', is a buddha's name. The other recension has skye 'chi med pas, with the same sense.

sentences.w: དེ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ བྱས་ ཆོག་གོ༔ རང་ གི་ ཤེས་རིགས་ ཀྱི་ ངོ་བོ༔ སང་ངེ་བ་ འདི་ སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ན༔ རང་ གི་ རིགས་པ་ ལ་ རང་ ལྟ་བ་ སྟེ༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཀྱི་ དགོངས་པ་ ལ་ འཇོག་པ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That face-knowing done, it-suffices. One's-own knowing-awareness's essence, open-clear, this, as-buddha face-know if: one's-own knowing at oneself looking is, and: the buddhas' mind in resting it-is.
sentences.i: To recognise this is enough. If you recognise the nature of your own clear, open awareness as the buddha, that is your own awareness looking at itself, and it is resting in the mind of the buddhas.
sentences.n: chog go, 'it will do', with the sentence-ending -go. The print writes shes rigs kyi, with an s that kyi agrees with, and rigs pa for rig pa; both are kept as printed and read as shes rig and rig pa, as everywhere else in the print and in the other recension. sangs rgyas su: su, 'as'.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ ལན་ གསུམ་མམ༔ བདུན་ གྱི་ བར་ ལ་ སྒྲ་ དག་ ལ་ ཚིག་ གསལ་བར་ བརྗོད་དོ༔
sentences.l: So, times three-or, seven's up-to, sound correct and words clearly, say.
sentences.i: Say this three or up to seven times, pronouncing it correctly and with every word distinct.
sentences.n: bdun gyi bar la, 'up to seven'. The other recension lacks tshig, 'words'.

sentences.w: དེས་ སྐད་ཅིག་ དང་པོ་ བླ་མས་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ལྟར་ དྲན་ ལ༔ གཉིས་པ་ རང་རིག་ རྗེན་པ་ འོད་གསལ་ དུ་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད༔ གསུམ་པ་ རང་ གི་ ཤེས་ ནས་ ཆོས་སྐུ་ འདུ་འབྲལ་ མེད་པར་ གྱུར་ ཏེ་ གྲོལ་བར་ ངེས་སོ༔ དེས་ འོད་གསལ་ དང་པོ་ ལ་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད༔
sentences.l: By-that: instant first, by-the-lama face-introduced like remembering, and; second, self-knowing bare as-clear-light face-meets; third, one's-own knowing, then, the body-of-truth, meeting-parting without having-become, and, freed certain-is. By-that, the clear-light first, at, the face-meets.
sentences.i: Through this, at the first instant he remembers what the lama pointed out; at the second he recognises his own bare awareness as the clear light; at the third, knowing it as his own, he becomes the body of truth, never to meet or part from it, and he is sure to be freed. So he recognises the first clear light.
sentences.n: rang rig, 'self-knowing', is awareness aware of itself. 'du 'bral med pa, 'without meeting or parting', is said of what was never two things. rang gi shes nas, 'knowing [it as] one's own', is thin; the other recension has rang ngo shes nas, 'recognising oneself', and ngo may have dropped out of this print. The translation follows the print. The other recension also words the first step differently, 'first he recalls what the lama pointed out before', without 'instant', and adds de grol lo, 'he is freed', after ngo 'phrod.

sentences.w: ཡང་ གལ་ཏེ་ འོད་གསལ་ དང་པོ་ དེ་ ལ་ ངོས་ མ་ ཟིན་ དོགས་ ན༔ ཡང་ འོད་གསལ་ གཉིས་པ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ འཆར་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Again, if, the clear-light first that at, recognition not seized fear if: again, clear-light second so-called dawns, and:
sentences.i: But if there is reason to fear that he has not recognised that first clear light, then what is called the second clear light dawns.
sentences.n: ngos zin, 'to seize the face', is another word for recognising. dogs, 'to fear, to suspect': dogs na, 'if it is feared that'. gal te ... na again brackets the condition.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ དུས་ ནི་ ཕྱི་དབུགས་ ཆད་ ནས་ ཟན་ ཅིག་ ཟ་ ཡུན་ ལྷག་ ཙམ་ སོང་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: That too, the time, as-for: the outer-breath having-stopped, then, meal one eating duration more about having-gone, then, comes.
sentences.i: It comes when a little more than the time it takes to eat a meal has passed since the outer breath stopped.
sentences.n: cig is gcig, 'one', in its softened form. lhag tsam, 'a little more'. 'ong ngo, 'comes', with the sentence-ending -ngo.

sentences.w: ལས་ བཟང་ངན་ གྱིས་ རྩ་ གཡས་ གཡོན་ གང་རུང་ གཅིག་ རླུང་ ཤོར་ ནས༔ སྒོ་ གང་རུང་ གཅིག་ ནས་ ཐོན༔ ཤེས་པ་ གསལ་ ལམ་གྱིས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Karma good-bad by: channels right, left, whichever one, the wind having-escaped: door whichever one from emerges. Consciousness clear in-a-flash comes.
sentences.i: Driven by good or bad karma, the wind escapes into one or other of the right and left channels and goes out by one or other of the body's openings, and consciousness suddenly becomes clear.
sentences.n: This is the escape into the side channels before which, the pilot said (p. 16), the first pointing-out must be given. shor, 'to slip away'. gang rung, 'whichever'. sgo, 'door', here the openings of the body. lam gyis, 'in a flash', as in the pilot.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ ཟན་ ཟ་ ཡུན་ ཟེར་ ཡང་ རྩ་ བཟང་ངན་ དང་༔ ཉམས་ལེན་ ཡོད་མེད་ དང་ བསྟུན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That too, meal eating duration say though, channels good-bad and, practice there-is-there-isn't, with conforms.
sentences.i: Though we say 'the time it takes to eat a meal', it depends on how sound the channels are and whether the person has practised.
sentences.n: dang bstun, 'to be in keeping with', so 'depends on'. yod med, 'there is, there is not': whether or not.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཚེ་ རྣམ་ཤེས་ ཕྱིར་ ཐོན་པ་ དང་༔ ཤི་བ་ ཡིན་ནམ་ མ་ ཤི་བ་ ཡིན་ སྙམ་དུ་ ངོ་ མི་ ཤེས།
sentences.l: That's time, the consciousness outward emerged as-soon-as: 'Dead is-it-or not dead is-it?' thinking, face not knows.
sentences.i: At that moment, as soon as the consciousness has come out, the dead person wonders, 'Am I dead or not?', and does not recognise what is happening.
sentences.n: rnam shes, 'consciousness', is what passes from life to life. yin nam, 'is it, or ...?': the 'or' ending in a question. The plain stroke ། closes this phrase, the mark of ordinary books, where the print elsewhere has ༔; it comes twice in this part.

sentences.w: ཉེ་དུ་ འབྲེལ་བ་ ཡང་ སྔར་ བཞིན་ མཐོང་ ནས་ ཡོད༔ དུ་རྒོད་ ཀྱང་ ཐོས་སོ༔
sentences.l: Relatives, connections too, before like, seeing is. Weeping(?)-laughing too hears.
sentences.i: He sees his relatives and friends as before, and hears their crying.
sentences.n: mthong nas yod, 'is seeing', the same spoken construction as 'char nas yod above. The print reads du rgod, which gives no sense; it is kept as printed. It is probably ngu rgod, 'weeping and laughing'; the other recension has ngu 'bod, 'weeping and wailing'. The translation takes it as crying, and is uncertain.

sentences.w: ལས་ ཀྱི་ འཁྲུལ་སྣང་ དྲག་པོ་ ཡང་ མ་ ཤར༔ གཤིན་རྗེའི་ འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ ཀྱང་ མ་ སླེབ་བའི་ བར་ དེར་ ཡང་ གདམས་ངག་ གདབ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Karma's delusive-appearances fierce too not arisen; the Lord-of-Death's terror too not arrived's interval, in-that too, instruction is-to-be-given, and:
sentences.i: The fierce visions that karma throws up have not yet arisen, and the terrors of the Lord of Death have not yet come. In this interval, too, the instruction is to be given.
sentences.n: 'khrul snang, 'deluded appearance', is what the mind sees when it takes its own projections for real. shar is the past of 'char, 'to arise'. gshin rje, 'Lord of the Dead' (Sanskrit Yama). sleb, 'to arrive', is a spoken word; sleb ba'i is the print's spelling of sleb pa'i. 'jigs is printed with one joined letter for its final gs; it is written out. The other recension has 'the wind of karma and the deluded appearances'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཡང་ རྫོགས་རིམ་པ་ དང་ བསྐྱེད་རིམ་པ་ གཉིས་སོ༔ རྫོགས་རིམ་པར་ ཡིན་ ན་ ནི་ མིང་ ནས་ ལན་ གསུམ་ འབོད་ ལ༔ གོང་ གི་ འོད་གསལ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ དེ་ སྐྱར་ ནས་ གདབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: That in too, completion-stage-one and generation-stage-one, two are. Completion-stage-one it-is if, as-for: by-name times three having-called, and, above's clear-light face-introduction that, having-repeated, is-to-be-given.
sentences.i: Here again there are two cases: those who practise the stage of completion and those who practise the stage of generation. For a practitioner of the completion stage, call him by name three times and give again the pointing-out of the clear light above.
sentences.n: In the generation stage (bskyed rim) one visualises oneself as a deity; in the completion stage (rdzogs rim) the visualisation dissolves and one rests in the mind's nature. -pa makes 'one who practises'. rdzogs rim par yin na has an -r one would not expect after the noun; it is kept as printed. ngo sprad, the past form, here 'that pointing-out'. skyar, 'repeat', as above.

sentences.w: བསྐྱེད་རིམ་ ཡིན་ ན་ ཁོང་རང་ གི་ ལྷ་ གང་ ཡིན་པ་ དེའི་ བསྒོམ་ཁོག་ དང་ བསྟུན་ ནས་ མངོན་རྟོགས་ ཀློགས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Generation-stage it-is if: his-own deity which is, its meditation-frame with having-conformed, the visualisation read, and:
sentences.i: If he practises the generation stage, read out the visualisation of whatever deity is his own, following the outline of its meditation, and say:
sentences.n: khong rang, 'he himself', the polite third person. bsgom khog, 'the frame of the meditation', its outline. mngon rtogs, 'clear realisation', is the text that describes the deity to be visualised. klogs is the imperative of klog, 'to read'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཡི་དམ་ འདི་ སྒོམས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཡེངས་ཤིག། འདུན་པ་ དྲག་པོ་ ཡི་དམ་ ལ་ གཏོད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! You-yourself's yidam this meditate! Not be-distracted! Aspiration fierce the yidam to direct!
sentences.i: O child of noble family, meditate on this, your own yidam. Do not be distracted. Turn a fierce longing toward your yidam.
sentences.n: yi dam is one's chosen deity, the one a practitioner meditates on above all. sgoms is the imperative of sgom, 'to meditate'; shig and cig are the same command particle as zhig, changing with the letter before. The plain stroke ། closes ma yengs shig.

sentences.w: སྣང་ ལ་ རང་བཞིན་ མེད་པ་ ཆུ་ཟླ་ ལྟ་བུར་ སྒོམས་ཤིག༔ གདོས་བཅས་ཅན་དུ་ མ་ སྒོམས་ཤིག༔ ཅེས་ གསལ་གདབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: Appearing and nature without, water-moon like, meditate! Material-having-as not meditate! So clear-remind.
sentences.i: Meditate on him as appearing, yet without any nature of his own, like the moon in water. Do not meditate on him as something solid. Remind him in this way.
sentences.n: The print writes can du as one stacked letter (ཅནྡུ), a contraction written out here; the letters of the stack are uncertain at the scan's resolution, though the sense is not. སྒོཾས, with a small circle for m, is likewise written out as sgoms. chu zla, 'water-moon', the moon reflected in water. gdos bcas, 'having matter'. The other recension is corrupt at this point.

sentences.w: སྐྱེ་བོ་ ཐ་མལ་པ་ ཡིན་ ན་ ཇོ་བོ་ ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་ སྒོམས་ཤིག༔ ཅེས་ ངོ་སྤྲད་དོ༔
sentences.l: A person ordinary it-is if: 'The Lord Great-Compassion meditate!' So face-introduce.
sentences.i: If he is an ordinary person, point it out with: 'Meditate on the Lord of Great Compassion.'
sentences.n: Thugs rje chen po, 'Great Compassion', is Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva of compassion; jo bo, 'lord'. tha mal pa, 'ordinary', one with no deity practice of his own.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པས་ བར་དོ་ ངོས་ མི་ ཟིན་པ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱང་ ཟིན་པར་ ཐེ་ཚོམ་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Thus face-introduced-by: the between recognition not seizing (plural) too, seizing, doubt there-is-not.
sentences.i: When it is pointed out like this, there is no doubt that even those who would not recognise the bardo will recognise it.
sentences.n: -pas on ngo sprad pa: 'by being pointed out'. zin par the tshom med, 'no doubt of seizing', the pilot's grol bar the tshom med.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ གསོན་བོའི་ དུས་སུ་ བླ་མས་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ གོམས་འདྲིས་ ཆུང་ ན་ བར་དོར་ རང་ གིས་ གསལ་ མི་ ཐེབས་པས༔ བླ་མའམ༔ མཆེད་གྲོགས་ ཀྱིས་ ངེས་པར་ གསལ་འདེབས་ དགོས་སོ༔
sentences.l: That too: living's time-at by-the-lama face-introduced though, familiarity small if, in-the-between by-oneself clarity not takes-hold because: a lama-or, a dharma-companion by, certainly clear-reminding is-needed.
sentences.i: Even if the lama pointed it out during life, a person who is little practised will not be able to make it clear for himself in the bardo, so a lama or a fellow disciple must remind him.
sentences.n: gson bo, 'living', is the print's spelling of gson po. goms 'dris, 'familiarity' (the pilot's print wrote gom 'dris). gsal mi thebs, 'the clearness does not take hold': thebs is the result of 'debs, so the reminder that others cast (gsal 'debs) must strike home in the dead person. The print writes 'debs at a line end with the s under the b (འདེབྶ); it is written out.

sentences.w: ཡང་ གོམས་འདྲིས་ ཡོད་ ཀྱང་ འཆི་ཁར་ ནད་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁྲུལ་ ནས༔ དྲན་པས་ མི་ ཟིན་པའི་ རིགས་ ལ་ ཡང་ གདམས་པ་ འདི་ ཤིན་ཏུ་ དགོས་སོ༔
sentences.l: Again, familiarity there-is though, at-the-point-of-death by-illness fierce having-been-confused: by-mindfulness not seizing's kinds for too, instruction this very needed-is.
sentences.i: Again, there are those who have practised but whose minds are thrown into confusion at death by severe illness, so that memory cannot hold on; for them too this instruction is most necessary.
sentences.n: 'chi khar, 'at the brink of death', 'chi kha with -r. nad drag pos: drag po, 'fierce', with -s, 'by', marking the cause. shin tu, 'very, extremely'.

sentences.w: སྔར་ ལམ་ གྱིས་ གོམས་འདྲིས་ ཡོད་ ཀྱང་༔ སྡོམ་པ་ ཤོར་བ་ དང་༔ རྩ་བའི་ དམ་ཚིག་ ཉམས་ ནས་ ངན་སོང་དུ་ འགྲོ་བའི་ རིགས་ ལ་ འདི་ ཅི་ནས་ཀྱང་ དགོས་སོ༔
sentences.l: Before, the path by, familiarity there-is though: vows having-slipped, and, root's vow-bonds having-declined, then, into-bad-destinies going's kinds for, this by-all-means needed-is.
sentences.i: And for those who practised the path before, but have let their vows slip and broken their root commitments, and so are headed for the lower realms, this is needed above all.
sentences.n: The print has ཤོར་བདང, a misprint for ཤོར་བ་དང, corrected here, as the other recension has it. dgos so is printed as one contracted syllable (དགོསོ) and written out. lam gyis is here 'by the path', practice, not 'in a flash'. rtsa ba'i dam tshig, 'the root commitments', are the vows of tantric practice. ngan song, 'bad goings', are rebirth as an animal, a hungry ghost or in hell. ci nas kyang, 'by all means'. The sentence goes on in the next part: the same print line ends with bar do, its first words.
